extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: A dataset consisting of 7,787 natural, grade-school science multiple-choice questions authored for standardized tests, partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set, along with the ARC Corpus of 14M science-related sentences and baseline models to encourage research in advanced question answering.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.citeAs: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord. Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457v1, 2018.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation to obtain publicly releasable natural science questions authored for standardized tests. Questions were drawn from a variety of sources and partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set. The Challenge Set was operationally defined as questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based solver and a pointwise mutual information solver. In addition, the ARC Corpus was created by using a major search engine to run a large series of automatically constructed science-related queries based on about 100 hand-written templates for 80 science topics, collecting top documents, de-duplicating them, stripping content to text, and chunking the text into sentences. The corpus was further augmented with the AristoMini corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The question set consists of natural science questions authored for use on standardized tests, drawn from sources such as state assessment programs, NAEP, TIMSS, and an anonymous AI2 content partner. The ARC Corpus consists of science-related web documents retrieved via a major search engine using automatically instantiated query templates, plus the AristoMini corpus containing dictionary definitions from Wiktionary, science-tagged Simple Wikipedia articles, and additional science sentences collected from the Web.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were sorted into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set based on whether two baseline solvers failed or succeeded. For the ARC Corpus, retrieved documents were de-duplicated, stripped down to text, and chunked into sentences. The corpus was augmented with AristoMini. In entailment-based baselines, questions and answer choices were converted into assertions, retrieved sentences were filtered for length, negation, and noise, and top sentences were selected.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus, the top several documents from each search were collected and de-duplicated, document content was stripped down to capture just the text, and the resulting text was chunked into sentences. For entailment baselines, questions were converted into fill-in-the-blank statements and then assertions with answer choices inserted. Retrieved sentences were required to contain the answer choice, and long sentences, sentences with negation, and noisy sentences were filtered out. The top 8 sentences across answer choices were selected as candidate premises.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper describes a categorization of knowledge and reasoning types based on a sample of 100 questions, requiring subjective judgment about the main challenge exhibited by different questions. It also states that the Science Entailment dataset used to train some baseline models was created in a similar manner where crowdworkers annotated premises and hypotheses as entailing or not. No human annotation protocol is described for labeling ARC questions themselves.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper notes that the categorization of knowledge and reasoning types is necessarily approximate because it requires subjective judgment about the main challenge exhibited by different questions. It also reports informal sampled analyses of corpus relevance, including that approximately 75% of a random sample of 805 collected documents were judged science relevant and that the ARC Corpus appears to mention knowledge relevant to approximately 95% of Challenge questions from a random sample.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, three baseline neural models, and leaderboard are available at http://data.allenai.org/arc. The paper also refers readers to the ARC leaderboard for up-to-date results.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Question grade level is included, ranging from 3rd grade to 9th, corresponding to students typically of age 8 through 13 years.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to encourage AI research on question answering that requires more powerful knowledge and reasoning than prior benchmarks, and to move the field away from overemphasis on surface-level retrieval methods.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper discusses that many prior QA datasets are biased toward retrieval-style questions solvable by surface-level cues, and that standardized test datasets can have scores dominated by simple algorithms, biasing research toward incremental improvements in retrieval and statistical correlation methods. For ARC baselines, the authors note retrieval bias toward sentences very similar to the question and away from sentences that only partially match individually but together explain the answer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The operational definition of Challenge questions only approximates the informal goal of being hard questions. The categorization of knowledge and reasoning types is approximate and subjective. The ARC Corpus contains relevant knowledge for many questions, but exploiting indirect mentions is not trivial, and the corpus does not solve the challenge of correctly identifying and reasoning with this knowledge or injecting unstated commonsense knowledge. The question-to-assertion conversion used in entailment baselines can produce non-grammatical sentences.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is presented as a challenge for advanced question answering research. It includes train/dev/test partitions for the Challenge and Easy sets, and baseline models are trained and evaluated on the dataset. The ARC Corpus is released as optional supporting text for corpus-based QA approaches; systems are not restricted to using this corpus.
